::: {.callout-warning}
## Superseded by Code Window

This extension is no longer developed.
[Code Window](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-code-window) replaces it: it labels code blocks with their language by default, and adds window-style decorations besides.

These pages document `language-cell-decorator` for the projects still using it, and describe the move.
:::

A code block in a Quarto document carries its language in a class, and shows it nowhere.
A reader scanning a page of examples has to infer from the syntax which language each block is written in.

`language-cell-decorator` put the name back on the block.

## Moving to Code Window

```bash
quarto remove mcanouil/quarto-language-cell-decorator
quarto add mcanouil/quarto-code-window
```

```yaml
filters:
  - path: code-window
    at: pre-quarto
```

Code Window shows the language by default, so nothing else is needed to get what this extension did.
Its own documentation covers the rest: <https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-code-window>.

## Installation

Still available, for projects that have not moved yet:

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

## Quick start

```yaml
filters:
  - language-cell-decorator
```

Then write code blocks as usual:

````markdown
```r
summary(cars)
```
````

```r
summary(cars)
```

The block above is decorated by the extension as this page renders.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for the filename label, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for blocks in several languages.

## Where it works

HTML formats, including RevealJS, draw the language above the block.
PDF turns the block into a code listing captioned with the language.
Typst and Word leave the block as it was.
